title: The 1956 trip to Europe with Armstrong
summary: Alcorn recounts sailing to Europe in 1956, Paris and Bechet, promoters counting standing crowds, and touring ten or twelve countries over the holidays.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Or it came through here in 1956. He was going to Europe. And Or it came by train from here to New York. He wouldn't ride the plane. He didn't get much for planes. He had to ride the plane later. So he came through here with his family. And he didn't get off the train. That's what I understand. This train went on New York. When I got to New York, I flew from here to New York. To go meet the ship. We went up on the SS plan. We was coming from different areas. Because we had taken a break. The band was off for a while. You see. We got this trip to go. And some of the guys came from California. They went direct from California to San Francisco and over. I came from New Orleans, New York and over. And that's the way I went. And Norrie came through here on the plane. I mean on a train. I went to New York with his family. And we all was on the same ship called SS Flammers.
And when was this? 1956. 1956. First trip he made over there.

Louis had been over there for years. You know, going back and forth. Bechet was over there. All of them were glad to see us when we got over. Sidney Bechet? Oh yeah, he was living there. Where did he live?

Paris. When I was close, he had a pillar out there. He was very popular. And we met promoters over there. Guys playing countries. The guy said one thing about Louis. He said, all we do is count the people standing up. We don't have to worry about this. Every seed is sold. Every time he plays. The guy in Paris told you this? Yeah. All over Europe. Everywhere Louis played. With Louis. He said, let's just pay four thousand people. It's four thousand people. See it. All he had to do is see how many are standing up. Count to one. Everything was a side seat. He was a natural man.

Never had a band concert. He was a favorite. The Europeans were crazy about that. Yeah. I know he lived in Paris. Yeah. He lived in Paris. Yeah. He lived in Paris. He lived in Paris. He lived in Paris. He lived in Paris. He lived in Paris.
He lived in Paris. ! 1934 I believe during the summer time.

Yeah, well he went over there and played and worked headquarter out of there. You see, the town of Haiti just like we headquartered out of there. We knew the Corporation of America, M.C.A. And that was our headquarters. We broke all around. I went around about ten, twelve countries. How long were you over there, 50 cents? We were supposed to stay five months or four months ago. I think we stayed about three months or four.
When did you go over there? What time of year?
Went over there almost this year.
Close to Christmas. Yeah, close to Christmas. November or something like that. And when did you come back? After New Years?

I think all of my holidays at that time, I think I was over there. I can remember getting a new feeling seeing the little Christmas decorations. Yeah. So used to celebrating it at home. Sure. But that was it. We were always over there. We wouldn't be in the same town or same state, the same country. We would be in Germany, we would be in England. Something like that. We would always know how to keep them things going.
